newsitem.title: USA: Israel's Meridor says economic slowdown temporary.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Meridor says economic slowdown temporary.

text.p: Strict fiscal discipline and tight monetary policy have contributed to the current slowing in Israel's economy, but the country's Finance Minister said the slowdown is thought to be only temporary.
"The slowdown in the economy is evident," said Dan Meridor, Israel's Finance Minister. But he added: "I do believe it is temporary."

Speaking to an Israeli investment conference here, Meridor told investors that Israel's economic growth could be less than 4.0 percent in 1997 but he added that the country's growth prospects will be clearer in about two to three months.
Meridor said he hopes the rate of inflation for Israel will come in between 7.0 to 10 percent in 1997.
Turning to the budget deficit, Meridor said: "We succeeded in cutting the budget deficit...setting the target in 1997, which will be around 2.8 percent of GDP."
But the Finance Minister added, "We still fight every day to keep the budget in line."
In the way of reforms, Meridor said the government is planning to move ahead with about 25 structural reforms.

Of those, he said the government is beginning the liberalization of the public transportation bus company. "We are in the process of opening this monopoly to competition. We are doing it gradually but it is a major change."

He also said the government is looking to do more in the way of privatizations. He said the government's Bank Leumi shares are up for sale and also added that El Al, the Israeli airline, needs to be sold.
"We have liberalized a lot and are still in the process."
In addition, Meridor said that there will be new public sector wage agreements in 1997.
"This year will be a year of new wage agreements in the public sector and these will have a dramatic effect if not conducted in the right way in coming years," he added.
As for the Middle East peace process, Meridor said it is important to build economic cooperation, economic stability and economic prosperity with Israel's neighbors.
"There is difficulty in the political process. We need to overcome that but a better economic sitution may help us all," he added.
